items.title: Live: Trump backflips on tolls, starts blockade and hits Iran again
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he will not charge a 20 per cent toll on traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, just hours before the US Navy's blockade is set to resume.

items.title: Telstra slammed for putting 'burden of proof on consumers' for compensation
items.description: Telstra is assessing outage compensation claims, but consumer advocates say the process is cumbersome and puts the onus on customers rather than the telco at fault.

items.title: Australia's highest paid CEO makes 500 times the average salary
items.description: Australia's highest-paid executive collected a salary nearly 500 times that of the country's full-time average worker.

items.title: Live: Spain into World Cup final with stunning upset over tournament favourite France
items.description: Spain is through to the World Cup final thanks to a 2-0 win over France. Follow live.

items.title: Anthony Albanese maps out AI future with new national framework
items.description: Labor will develop a new national framework in response to artificial intelligence as it seeks to address the technology’s growing economic and social impacts.

items.title: Live: Minister pushes back on calls to cut tobacco excise as black market grows
items.description: Clare O'Neil says reducing the tobacco excise to address the rising take-up of illicit tobacco will not help Australians give up smoking. Follow live.

items.title: What Australia's economy could look like under One Nation
items.description: From interest rates to policy advice from billionaire buddy Gina Rinehart, here is how One Nation's economic platform could look.

items.title: Jewish student tells of her disgust at TikToks in Auschwitz car park
items.description: Paris Enten has told the antisemitism royal commission her experiences of Monash University, including during an overseas trip, caused her mental health to deteriorate.

items.title: Bali-based businessman's death leaves Australians chasing money
items.description: Cameron Hughes, 39, died in a Balinese immigration detention centre last week under yet-to-be-confirmed circumstances. The ABC can reveal the Perth businessman left behind hundreds of thousands of dollars in unfinished business, with dozens of customers potentially out of pocket.

items.title: As Japan undergoes a defence shift, China warns it's 'becoming a powder keg'
items.description: While the world has been watching the rise of China, Japan has been in the midst of its biggest defence shift since World War II.

items.title: Brisbane's lower clearance rate shows a 'disconnect' between buyers and sellers
items.description: After a decades-long real estate boom, experts say the balance of power is finally shifting from sellers to buyers.

items.title: The Thai child sex exploitation scourge unfolding at bars, restaurants and hotels
items.description: Thailand is struggling against a "hidden" world of child sexual exploitation that requires action from both the tourism industry and law enforcement agencies, according to NGOs.

items.title: Batteries charge ahead as data centres fuel gas turbine costs: CSIRO
items.description: Falling battery costs and a data centre-fuelled dash for gas have overturned decades of accepted wisdom: gas is no longer the cheapest way to meet peak power demand.

items.title: Smart glasses help vision-impaired despite privacy concerns
items.description: For people who are blind, AI-powered smart glasses deliver a level of independence that was once out of reach, but the rise of wearable cameras also raises urgent questions about surveillance, consent and the law.

items.title: No fee, no sign-in: The art class removing 'barriers' to recovery
items.description: In regional NSW, one program shows that creativity may be the key to better mental health.

items.title: Monet, Renoir, van Gogh masterpieces appear in two new blockbuster exhibitions
items.description: More than 150 years after the first Impressionist exhibition in Paris, the Art Gallery of South Australia and Geelong Gallery cast new light on the influential art movement.

items.title: Quiz: Dust off your passport and join us on a trip
items.description: Which of these peaks isn't in the Himalayas? And in what country would you find the island of Rapa Nui?

items.title: Tourists turn away from NT as Kakadu travellers greeted by closure signs
items.description: It is known as the jewel in the Northern Territory's tourism crown, but visitors to Kakadu National Park are being greeted by closure signs blocking roads to key waterfall sites.

items.title: Tasmanian government proposes buying Boag's Brewery site
items.description: The Tasmanian government wants to buy Launceston's Boag's Brewery site and says it has "in-principle" support from the Japanese parent company to explore the idea.

items.title: Scale of Australia's shortage of child psychiatrists revealed in new report
items.description: Experts are warning younger children are presenting with increasingly complex mental health needs as a new report predicts a nationwide shortfall of child and adolescent psychiatrists.

items.title: Natural nanotech the new weapon against flystrike
items.description: A biopesticide using tea-tree oil in nanoparticles has been developed to keep flies off sheep.

items.title: 'I'm ruling it out': Taylor categorically kills off One Nation coalition talk
items.description: Coalition leader Angus Taylor has renewed his criticism of Pauline Hanson's party and categorically ruled out any alliance with it.

items.title: Suspected Widdecombe murder being treated as a targeted attack
items.description: After initially saying the alleged murder of British former politician Ann Widdecombe was not politically motivated, police now say they believe it was a targeted attack.

items.title: Woman sues ex-Catholic archbishop over alleged abuse by another priest
items.description: A Tasmanian woman is suing former Archbishop of Hobart Julian Porteous and the state of Tasmania over allegations of sexual abuse by two others when she was a child.

items.title: Calls for memorial for 151 fallen miners go unheard
items.description: For decades, families of Mount Isa miners killed on the job have waited for a lasting tribute, but after years of campaigning, some fear their loved ones will be forgotten.
